# PLAN — iteration 1
## Current state assessment
The verified incumbent is timing-feasible at 68 LUTs, 81 FFs, WNS 0.302 ns and WHS 0.185 ns, with the trusted simulation passing. The core keeps separate WIDTH-bit dividend and quotient shift registers; the objective is to reduce LUTs, with fewer FFs as a tie-break when LUT count is unchanged. Preserve the top’s `// @latency 9` annotation and the specified schedule, handshakes, reset behavior, and WIDTH 1–16 arithmetic.

## Hypothesis
Using one WIDTH-bit register first to shift out dividend bits and then to accumulate quotient bits should remove WIDTH FFs and may reduce associated LUT logic without changing the iterative arithmetic or cycle schedule.

## Instruction for generator
In `iterative_divider_core`, remove `dividend_shift` and use `quotient_work` as the combined shift register: load the captured dividend into it, take each trial remainder’s next bit from its MSB, then shift left and append the computed quotient bit. Keep the WIDTH+1-bit trial remainder, one arithmetic iteration on each of the WIDTH compute edges, and the registered final outputs; express shifts so WIDTH=1 has no negative part-select. Preserve the zero-divisor result, stall stability, reset abort, and the retirement-edge readiness bubble; retain the top interface and `// @latency 9`.
